notes.text: Infinitely often a — GF a. The machine sits in "saw a" exactly after each a, so the one deterministic run passes through F infinitely often precisely when the word has infinitely many a's. No guessing is needed anywhere, so this ω-language is deterministic-Büchi recognisable.

Now compare its mirror image. GF a is a DBA language; FG b ("eventually always b") is not — no DBA recognises it, though an NBA does. That gap is real: deterministic Büchi automata capture exactly the limits of regular languages, a proper subset of the ω-regular ones. Load the Büchi model's "eventually always b" example to see the machine that needs the guess.

meta.title: Classic: infinitely often a
meta.blurb: GF a, the canonical deterministic Büchi automaton. Its mirror FG b is the standard witness that DBAs are strictly weaker than NBAs.
